title: IB Introduction
subject: IB Introduction
description_short: Explore the IB philosophy and methodology while sampling classes in Literature, Language, Maths, Theatre, Humanities, Science and Theory of Knowledge.
description_full: Explore the IB philosophy and methodology while sampling classes in Literature, Language, Maths, Theatre, Humanities, Science and Theory of Knowledge.

curriculum_sections.title: Course benefits
curriculum_sections.body: IB Methodology Understand the IB philosophy and methodology, laying a strong foundation for future IB Diploma success. Excellent Preparation for the IB Diploma Gain subject knowledge and skills across English Literature, English Language, Maths, Performing Arts, Humanities, Science and the ‘Theory of Knowledge’ - aligned with the IB Diploma curriculum. Specialist IB Teaching Learn from highly experienced IB teachers at England’s longest established IB World School, with 50 years of expertise. Critical Thinking Discover the Theory of Knowledge (TOK), developing essential skills in critical thinking, analysis and international mindedness. Hands-On Learning & Study Visits Enhance classroom learning with engaging Study Visits, such as to Bletchley Park and the Shakespeare Open-Air Theatre, connecting theory with real-world academic and cultural experiences. Collaborative Projects Work in small teams on a subject-based project, developing teamwork, problem-solving and cross-cultural understanding. Small Class Sizes & Supportive Environment With a maximum of 12 students per class, you’ll benefit from personalised support and close interaction with subject specialists. Beyond the Classroom Enrich your experience with sports, cultural and social activities and excursions and a careers advice session to guide your academic journey. EMA ARGENTINA, IB INTRODUCTION 2022 "I love the creativity in which the lessons are given, the teaching style is very dynamic. The teachers are very nice and they make sure everyone understands.” Explore the IB philosophy and methodology while sampling classes in Literature, Language, Maths, Theatre, Humanities, Science and Theory of Knowledge. Apply multi-disciplinary learning through an in-depth study of Shakespeare across history, literature and the performing arts. Study Visits and Guest Speakers Being based in the academic city of Oxford gives students access to an exciting programme of Guest Speakers and Study Visits. Recent speakers include Dr Tom Crawford (PhD Applied Mathematics, Cambridge), Christian Adofo (Nike Journalist & Brand Creative Writer) and Dr Marcus Nyman (Senior Policy Officer, RSPB; PhD Geography, Cambridge). Study visits have taken students to the Bletchley Park, a Shakespeare play at the Open-Air Theatre and Christchurch College, offering rich learning beyond the classroom. Careers Advice Session Our IB Introduction course includes a dedicated Careers Advice session, where students meet with our experienced University and Career Counsellors to explore future pathways, university options and career opportunities. This guidance helps students make informed decisions and plan their next steps with confidence. COURSE STRUCTURE DISCOVER More

title: Intensive English Exam Prep
subject: Intensive English Exam Prep
description_short: Improve your chances of success and prepare for your IELTS or Cambridge English examinations by learning exam tips, practising exam techniques and developing academic study skills.
description_full: Improve your chances of success and prepare for your IELTS or Cambridge English examinations by learning exam tips, practising exam techniques and developing academic study skills.

curriculum_sections.title: Course benefits
curriculum_sections.body: Develop Confiedence in Exams Build exam skills for IELTS or the Cambridge English exams, with focused tips, exam practice and develop strategies to maximise your performance. Prepare for Academic Study Strengthen essential skills – critical thinking, essay writing, research, presentations and debate – that will support your future studies. Personal Research Project Work independently on a project that develops your research skills and prepares you for the demands of higher education. Inspiring Guest Speakers and Guest Visits Learn beyond the classroom with visits to Oxford’s academic resources and talks from professionals who connect theory to real-world practice. Careers Advice Session Gain practical guidance from our University and Career counselling team on career pathways related to your course, helping you plan for your academic and professional future. Small Class Sizes & Quality Support Study in classes of up to 12 students, ensuring personalised feedback, encouragement and focused academic support. Learning Resources Take advantage of our library with access to a large collection of books, journals and newspapers spread across 4 storeys and browse through the resources handpicked by our librarian that are related to the weekly theme. More Than Just Studying Enjoy a balance of academics and fun, with sports, activities and excursions to London, cultural landmarks, heritage sites and theme parks. DOROTA POLAND, INTENSIVE ENGLISH 2022 " Having to speak English at St Clare’s, definitely helped me improve it. I learned many new idioms and specific English expressions during class which not only helped my speaking but also my writing. ” Improve your chances of success and prepare for your IELTS or Cambridge English examinations by learning exam tips, practising exam techniques and developing academic study skills. Study Visits and Guest Speakers Being based in the academic city of Oxford gives students access to an exciting programme of Guest Speakers and Study Visits. Recent speakers include Dr Tom Crawford (PhD Applied Mathematics, Cambridge), Christian Adofo (Nike Journalist & Brand Creative Writer) and Dr Marcus Nyman (Senior Policy Officer, RSPB; PhD Geography, Cambridge). Study visits have taken students to the Ashmolean Museum, North Wall Gallery and a local nature reserve, offering rich learning beyond the classroom. COURSE STRUCTURE DISCOVER

title: Interactive English
subject: Interactive English
description_short: Increase your fluency and confidence through language projects, guest speakers and study visits, all linked to varied, topical weekly themes.
description_full: Increase your fluency and confidence through language projects, guest speakers and study visits, all linked to varied, topical weekly themes.

curriculum_sections.title: Course benefits
curriculum_sections.body: Gain Confidence in English Improve all four key skills – listening, speaking, reading and writing – while building vocabulary, accuracy and fluency. Active Language Projects Learn through engaging Weekly Themes that connect classroom work with the inspiring academic city of Oxford. Dynamic Academic Programme Be inspired by Study Visits and Guest Speakers connected to the weekly theme. Active Language Project Develop your language skills through projects designed to maximise language usage, teamwork and collaboration. Small Classes and Quality Teaching Study in classes of up to 15 students with qualified, experienced English teachers who provide individual support. Supportive and Diverse Environment Learn in a safe, welcoming setting alongside classmates from around the world, building cultural awareness and lifelong friendships. Memorable Experiences Beyond the Classroom Enjoy a full activities and excursions programme, including arts and crafts, a variety of sports and social activities, excursions to places of historical and cultural interest in Oxford and the UK, as well as fun trips to theme parks and water parks. Study in an Inspiring Location Oxford’s history, architecture and global reputation for innovation provide a unique and motivating environment for your studies. ANNA GERMANY, INTERACTIVE ENGLISH 2022 " I really like the classes at St Clare's because the teachers are enthusiastic and they encourage you to speak English and to try new things like group activities. That’s why I really enjoy my time here! ” Increase your fluency and confidence through language projects, guest speakers and study visits, all linked to varied, topical weekly themes. Study Visits and Guest Speakers Being based in the academic city of Oxford gives students access to an exciting programme of Guest Speakers and Study Visits. Recent speakers include Dr Tom Crawford (PhD Applied Mathematics, Cambridge), Christian Adofo (Nike Journalist & Brand Creative Writer) and Dr Marcus Nyman (Senior Policy Officer, RSPB; PhD Geography, Cambridge). Study visits have taken students to the Ashmolean Museum, Natural History Museum, Modern Art Oxford, guided tours of the local nature reserve and workshops with local artists at The North Wall Gallery. title: Science & Experiments
subject: Science & Experiments
description_short: Develop practical investigative science skills using data logging machines and microscopes, explore the University of Oxford’s scienced-themed museums and learn about research methodology. Apply your knowledge by conducting a scientific research project and presenting your findings.
description_full: Develop practical investigative science skills using data logging machines and microscopes, explore the University of Oxford’s scienced-themed museums and learn about research methodology. Apply your knowledge by conducting a scientific research project and presenting your findings.

curriculum_sections.title: Course benefits
curriculum_sections.body: Focus on Core Sciences Explore key topics in Biology, Chemistry and Physics, developing both subject knowledge and scientific vocabulary in English. Prepare for Further Study Build the practical investigative skills you’ll need for future studies in science, supported by staff with international teaching experience. Learn in State-of-the-Art Laboratories Use specialist equipment such as data logging machines and microscopes in modern, fully equipped science labs. Gain Hands-On Laboratory Experience Master essential techniques: observation, measuring, controlling variables, recording results and evaluating conclusions. Meet Practising Scientists Be inspired by Guest Speakers who share their cutting-edge research and insights from the world of science. Stimulating Study Visits Connect classroom learning with real-world science through visits to Oxford’s Natural History Museum, Pitt Rivers Museum, History of Science Museum and the University of Oxford Botanical Gardens. Personal Research Project Investigate a topic of your choice, conduct experiments and present your findings – building critical research and presentation skills. Supportive Environment & Future Pathways Study in small, supportive classes with a high staff-to-student ratio, enjoy excursions and cultural activities and receive tailored careers advice to guide your next steps in science. POVILAS LITHUANIA, SCIENCE & EXPERIMENTS 2025 " We don't just learn, we also develop different research projects and experiments which is really exciting. ” Develop practical investigative science skills using data logging machines and microscopes, explore the University of Oxford’s scienced-themed museums and learn about research methodology. Apply your knowledge by conducting a scientific research project and presenting your findings. Study Visits and Guest Speakers Being based in the academic city of Oxford gives students access to an exciting programme of Guest Speakers and Study Visits. Recent speakers include Dr Tom Crawford (PhD Applied Mathematics, Cambridge), Christian Adofo (Nike Journalist & Brand Creative Writer) and Dr Marcus Nyman (Senior Policy Officer, RSPB; PhD Geography, Cambridge). Study visits have taken students to Oxford’s Natural History Museum, Pitt Rivers Museum, History of Science Museum and the University of Oxford Botanical Gardens, offering rich learning beyond the classroom. Careers Advice Session Our Science & Experiments course includes a dedicated Careers Advice session, where students meet with our experienced University and Career Counsellors to explore future pathways, university options and career opportunities in the sciences. This guidance helps students make informed decisions and plan their next steps with confidence. title: Young Leaders
subject: Young Leaders
description_short: Learn about global challenges facing leaders of the future, while developing leadership, critical thinking skills, resilience and mindfulness.
description_full: Learn about global challenges facing leaders of the future, while developing leadership, critical thinking skills, resilience and mindfulness.

curriculum_sections.title: Course benefits
curriculum_sections.body: Develop Leadership Skills Build confidence, resilience and mindfulness while developing the critical thinking and leadership qualities needed for the future. Tackle Global Challenges Explore real-world global challenges such as climate change, international relations and the impact of emerging technologies. Small Classes, Big Impact Enjoy the advantages of a small class size, with more individual support and chances to work closely with other students on projects. Master Communication Sharpen your presentation, teamwork and public speaking skills through group projects, presentations and a public speaking workshop. Get Adventurous Spend a day in the great outdoors, taking part in an orienteering challenge, hiking and an overnight camp out. Thriving International Atmosphere Join students from a range of countries and cultures, creating stimulating discussions and a lively, multicultural learning environment. Support Every Step of the Way Enjoy 24/7 support from our friendly and caring team and our team of residential activity leaders lead an action-packed activities programme and accompany you on excursions. Study in Oxford Live and learn in the world-famous city of Oxford, with up to 3 excursions per week to cultural and historical landmarks across the UK. title: Esports in Motorsport
subject: Engineering
description_short: One week with Dallara and AK Esports, from the simulator to the real track at the home of American motorsport.
description_full: Esports in Motorsport: Sim to Reality This esports and sim racing summer program in Indianapolis runs for one week and is designed for students aged 15 to 18. Designed for students passionate about motorsport, engineering and sim racing. Hosted at Dallara AK Esports’ Indianapolis facilities during US spring break, this one-week program puts students inside the loop real race engineers live in: make performance decisions first in the simulator, then validate them against the real car, the factory and the Indianapolis Motor Speedway. It complements our Engineering & Technologies in Motorsport program at Dallara in Italy: together, a two-campus Dallara Pathway from building a race car to engineering its performance. In Indianapolis the Dallara Experience Hub, the Dallara IndyCar Factory and the Speedway sit within reach of one another: the simulator and the real car it models quite literally share an address.

curriculum_sections.title: Curriculum
curriculum_sections.body: Simulation & Performance Engineering • Vehicle dynamics, aerodynamics and setup applied hands-on in the simulator, working towards a measurable performance gain over a baseline. • Data, Telemetry & Race Strategy • Telemetry, data analysis and race strategy: reading the numbers the way a race engineer does and turning them into decisions. • Sim-to-Reality Correlation & Race Weekend Capstone • Understanding the levels of fidelity from a gaming simulator to a professional driver-in-the-loop simulator to the track, then validating the work against reality. • Special Excursions • Tour of the Dallara US Factory & Experience Hub, the Indianapolis Motor Speedway and a team dinner. • Final Project • The program culminates in a virtual race weekend: teams apply their setup, strategy and telemetry work, then validate the result against the real IR-18 chassis, Dallara’s own sim-to-reality correlation process and published Speedway lap data.

curriculum_sections.title: Program highlights
curriculum_sections.body: Vehicle dynamics, aerodynamics and setup in a professional simulator • Telemetry, data and race strategy applied to a real chassis • Sim-to-reality correlation and a virtual race weekend capstone

learning_outcomes: Vehicle dynamics, aerodynamics and setup in a professional simulator
Telemetry, data and race strategy applied to a real chassis
Sim-to-reality correlation and a virtual race weekend capstone

title: Architecture & Urban Design
subject: Design
description_short: Studio work and site visits across Milan, from historic buildings to the districts being redrawn today.
description_full: This architecture and urban design summer program in Milan runs for two weeks and is designed for students aged 15 to 18. Designed for aspiring architects and urban designers alike. Hosted in Milan, the world capital of design, this two-week program takes students across every scale of the discipline, from buildings and open spaces to infrastructure. Working in hands-on studios led by leading architects and designers, participants sketch, model and prototype, culminating in a capstone that reimagines a run-down urban area as their own renovation concept. The program takes place in Milan, the global capital of design and a world reference point for architecture and interiors. Home to Salone del Mobile, Milan Design Week and the ADI Design Museum, the city is where design culture is made. Students work alongside practicing architects and designers, and visit iconic urban renovations that have attracted international attention.

curriculum_sections.title: Curriculum
curriculum_sections.body: Urban & Architectural Design Foundations • Explore architecture and design at every scale through studio work, lectures and project-based learning, starting from the fundamentals of urban and architectural design. • Sketching & Model Making • Develop skills in sketching and model-making, studying how exterior spaces are conceived and composed. • 3D Design & Digital Concepts • Move from hand drawing to 3D design and digital concepts, translating ideas into presentable models. • Special Excursions • Visits to urban requalifications in Milan such as Scalo Farini, Porta Genova and Scalo Romana, plus a Lake Como excursion. • Final Project • The program culminates in a capstone project: students reimagine a run-down urban area, from concept and sketches to a portfolio-ready renovation proposal.

curriculum_sections.title: Program highlights
curriculum_sections.body: Learn the fundamentals of urban and architectural design • Develop skills in sketching, model-making and 3D digital concepts • Reimagine a run-down urban area in a portfolio-ready renovation project

learning_outcomes: Learn the fundamentals of urban and architectural design
Develop skills in sketching, model-making and 3D digital concepts
Reimagine a run-down urban area in a portfolio-ready renovation project

title: Automotive Design
subject: Transportation Design
description_short: Car design with Alfa Romeo and Pagani: sketching, clay modelling and a full project brief.
description_full: Automotive Design & Future Mobility This automotive and car design summer program in Milan runs for two weeks and is designed for students aged 15 to 18. An immersive two-week program introducing the fundamentals of automotive design through studio work, clay modelling, digital tools and curated industry visits in Milan, Turin and Motor Valley. Students work in modern labs equipped with professional software for sketching, digital rendering and clay modelling, then extend the experience to Turin, the historic heart of Italian automotive culture, and to Motor Valley.

curriculum_sections.title: Curriculum
curriculum_sections.body: Design Foundations & Sketching • Develop sketching techniques and understand vehicle proportions through studio-based learning in modern labs. • Digital Rendering & Basic 3D Exploration • Translate ideas into digital renders using professional software, exploring basic 3D. • Clay Modelling & Industry Experience • Experiment with clay modelling and volume development, with curated industry experience. • Special Excursions • Motor Valley (Dallara and Pagani Automobili), National Automotive Museum and ADI Museum. • Final Project • The program culminates in the development and presentation of a personal automotive concept, including refined sketches, a digital render and a 1:10 scale clay model.

curriculum_sections.title: Program highlights
curriculum_sections.body: Car design foundations, sketching and vehicle proportions • Clay modelling, volume development and 1:10 scale model creation • Digital rendering, basic 3D exploration and future mobility concepts

learning_outcomes: Car design foundations, sketching and vehicle proportions
Clay modelling, volume development and 1:10 scale model creation
Digital rendering, basic 3D exploration and future mobility concepts

title: Biomedical Engineering
subject: Engineering
description_short: Where engineering meets medicine: prosthetics, imaging and the devices that keep people alive.
description_full: This biomedical engineering summer program in Milan runs for two weeks and is designed for students aged 15 to 18. Designed for students fascinated by the meeting point of medicine and engineering. Hosted in Milan, Italy’s hub for healthcare, life sciences and biomedical innovation, this two-week program shows how medical technology is designed, prototyped and tested, and ends with a capstone project developed together with a biomedical engineering company. The program takes place in Milan, the heart of Italy’s healthcare and life sciences ecosystem, a city with world-class hospitals, research universities and a dense network of medtech and biotech companies. Here students study in a real academic environment, working in engineering labs alongside researchers and industry professionals.

curriculum_sections.title: Curriculum
curriculum_sections.body: Foundations: Medical Devices & Biomechanics • Learn how medical devices work and how the mechanics of the human body shape their design. • Biotechnology, Diagnostics & Prototyping • Explore biotechnology and diagnostics, and build and prototype your own medical device. • Testing, Industry & Capstone Project • Test and validate your prototype, meet the industry and develop the capstone with a biomedical engineering company. • Special Excursions • Company visits to medtech and biotech companies, a Lake Como excursion and Milan sightseeing (residential only). • Capstone Project with the Industry • The program culminates in a capstone project developed together with a biomedical engineering company.

curriculum_sections.title: Program highlights
curriculum_sections.body: Medical devices and the biomechanics of the human body • Biotechnology, diagnostics and hands-on prototyping • Testing, industry visits and a capstone project

learning_outcomes: Medical devices and the biomechanics of the human body
Biotechnology, diagnostics and hands-on prototyping
Testing, industry visits and a capstone project

title: Business
subject: Business
description_short: The business behind Italian luxury, taught inside the maisons, showrooms and shipyards that built it.
description_full: Business of Luxury Goods This business summer program in Milan runs for two weeks and is designed for students aged 15 to 18. The Italian Business Excellence Management (IBEM) program has a strong focus on the luxury sector, where Italian companies excel: Fashion, Automotive, Yachting, Jewelry & Watches, and Hospitality. Unlike traditional business summer programs, ours is extremely hands-on, built to teach skills you won’t find in university textbooks. Students learn the “Made in Italy” managerial model directly from top executives and founders, through company visits, applied workshops and a real business challenge. The IBEM is headquartered in the heart of Milan, Italy’s economic and financial capital, hosting the stock exchange, major banks, numerous multinational HQs, and a significant portion of Italy’s GDP. Students alternate in-class lectures walking distance from their accommodation with company and innovation district visits across Northern Italy, the country’s primary industrial and economic powerhouse.

curriculum_sections.title: Curriculum
curriculum_sections.body: Leadership & Entrepreneurial Mindset • Students build a strong foundation in Italian business management: leadership, strategy and the organizational models that drive excellence in Italian enterprises, starting from an introduction to business management and entrepreneurship. • Strategy, Finance & Internationalization • Leadership, strategy and sustainability are explored alongside the financial and international dimensions of running a luxury business. • Industry Deep Dive • Exclusive company visits, applied workshops and direct interaction with industry leaders show how Italy’s luxury industries turn strategy, craftsmanship and innovation into globally recognized success. • Special Excursions • Company visits to Pagani, Baglietto, Pomellato and other leading Italian brands, plus a Lake Como excursion, pizza night and an Italian lunch. • Final Project • Everything culminates in a final group project: students start their own business from scratch and pitch it.

curriculum_sections.title: Program highlights
curriculum_sections.body: Leadership & entrepreneurial mindset • Strategy, finance & internationalization • Industry deep dive & real business project

learning_outcomes: Leadership & entrepreneurial mindset
Strategy, finance & internationalization
Industry deep dive & real business project

Discover the world of Business of Luxury Goods at the heart of Italy’s most prestigious institutions and companies. Students work inside real business environments, alongside practising professionals, using the same tools, methodologies and approaches as the actual industry. In collaboration with Spring Studios, Baglietto, Pagani and Cipriani, this programme offers a unique blend of hands-on learning, expert mentorship and immersive cultural experience in Milan. All teaching is in English. Ideal for Business, Management, Marketing, Economics and Luxury/Fashion Management students. title: Cosmetic Sciences
subject: Health & Life Sciences
description_short: Cosmetic formulation with Universita di Pavia, from the lab bench to the beauty industry that sells it.
description_full: This cosmetic sciences summer program in Milan runs for two weeks and is designed for students aged 15 to 18. Designed for students fascinated by the science and business of beauty. Hosted in Milan, this two-week program explores how cosmetics are formulated, tested and brought to market, from the chemistry of ingredients to AI-driven formulation and the trends reshaping the global beauty industry. Hands-on lab work lets students create their own products, from molecules to finished formula. The program takes place in Milan, the world capital of fashion and beauty and the gateway to Italy’s cosmetics industry, one of the world’s leading centres for cosmetics and make-up manufacturing. Here students study in a real academic environment, accessing the labs of one of the world’s leading cosmetics universities, Università di Pavia, with hands-on access to formulation and testing laboratories.

curriculum_sections.title: Curriculum
curriculum_sections.body: Formulation Chemistry & Product Development • Learn the fundamentals of formulation chemistry and product development, and work hands-on in the lab to create your own skincare and make-up. • Testing, Efficacy & Safety + AI • Explore how products are tested for efficacy and safety, including the growing role of AI in formulation. • Beauty Trends & Innovation • Decode the trends reshaping the global market, from skin longevity and K-Beauty to the science and storytelling of ingredients. • Special Excursions • Company visits to Italy’s leading cosmetic companies, a Lake Como excursion and Milan sightseeing (residential only), plus pizza night. • From Molecules to Finished Formula • Hands-on lab work lets students create their own products, from molecules to finished formula.

curriculum_sections.title: Program highlights
curriculum_sections.body: Formulate skincare and make-up in the lab • AI-powered formulation, testing and safety • Decode beauty trends: skin longevity, K-Beauty, ingredients

learning_outcomes: Formulate skincare and make-up in the lab
AI-powered formulation, testing and safety
Decode beauty trends: skin longevity, K-Beauty, ingredients

title: Fashion
subject: Fashion
description_short: Two weeks inside Milan fashion, from studio and atelier work to the industry that turns it into a collection.
description_full: This fashion summer program in Milan runs for two weeks and is designed for students aged 15 to 18. An immersive two-week program in Milan, the global fashion capital, taking students on the full journey of launching their own fashion brand: from the first sketch to a finished garment, a brand identity and lookbook, and a go-to-market launch with a social media page and website mockup. Students work in professional fashion and photography studios in the heart of Milan, surrounded by the ateliers, showrooms and flagship stores of the Quadrilatero della Moda, where global fashion is actually made.

curriculum_sections.title: Curriculum
curriculum_sections.body: Design & Create Your Garment • Design and create your own garment, from the first sketch and tailoring to a finished piece, while learning styling and editorial shooting. • Brand Identity & Lookbook • Build a brand around your garment: choose a name, develop its identity and produce a professional lookbook. • Launch to Market & Industry Immersion • Take your label to market: develop a social media page, a website mockup and a launch campaign, with company visits to leading Italian fashion houses. • Special Excursions • Giorgio Armani Prive visit, leading fashion brands visits and a gelato afternoon in Milan. • Final Project • The program culminates in the launch of a complete fashion label: a finished garment, a brand identity and lookbook, and a go-to-market campaign with social media and website mockup.

curriculum_sections.title: Program highlights
curriculum_sections.body: Design and create your own garment, from sketch and tailoring to a finished piece • Build a brand: name, identity and a professional lookbook • Launch to market with a social media page, website mockup and campaign

title: Football - AC Milan Experience Elite
subject: Sports
description_short: Train with AC Milan Academy coaches inside the club’s elite facilities, with the same methodology and video analysis used by the academy.
description_full: AC Milan Academy Experience Élite This football summer camp in Milan is open to students aged 8 to 16, for one or two weeks. Train under AC Milan’s official Youth Team coaches at the club’s iconic Vismara training center, home to the Puma House of Football. A true Rossoneri experience built on 125 years of footballing excellence. Players train inside AC Milan’s elite facilities (7 training pitches, changing rooms, gym and recovery areas) using the same methodology, GPS tracking and video analysis as the Rossoneri youth academy.

curriculum_sections.title: Curriculum
curriculum_sections.body: Monday • Reception & evaluation. Registration and camp presentation. Athletic tests, technical analysis and first training session: ball control and dribbling. • Tuesday-Wednesday • Technique & tactics. 1v1 game situations, intensive training with GPS tracking, role-specific and individual technique sessions with custom video analytics. • Thursday • Development & competition. Leadership work on the pitch, mental coaching, recovery and injury-prevention techniques, set-piece sessions. • Friday • Optimization & competition. Individual work with AC Milan technicians, personalized performance feedback and progress review. • Weekend (Residential) • Final tournament & celebration. Awards and individual recognition, Meet & Greet with AC Milan Legends, excursions to Casa Milan, Milan sightseeing and Lake Como.

curriculum_sections.title: Program highlights
curriculum_sections.body: 30+ hours of coaching with official AC Milan Academy coaches • Exclusive access to the Puma House of Football, Vismara • Meet & Greet with AC Milan Legends and Casa Milan visit

learning_outcomes: 30+ hours of coaching with official AC Milan Academy coaches
Exclusive access to the Puma House of Football, Vismara
Meet & Greet with AC Milan Legends and Casa Milan visit

title: Medicine
subject: Health & Life Sciences
description_short: Hands-on clinical and laboratory learning at San Raffaele University, one of Italy’s most prestigious medical institutions.
description_full: This medicine summer program in Milan runs for two weeks and is designed for students aged 15 to 18. The Medicine Summer Program, with academic coordination by Università Vita-Salute San Raffaele (UniSR), is designed for motivated high school students who are considering a future in medicine or healthcare. Through direct training with doctors and specialists, participants gain early exposure to medical practice and develop essential skills in diagnostics, emergency response and patient care. The program takes place at UniSR, a leading medical school in Italy known for its integration of teaching and research. The university is closely affiliated with the San Raffaele Research Hospital, a pioneer in cutting-edge medical and scientific research. UniSR ranks among the top 40 universities in the world and offers a 6-year International MD program.

curriculum_sections.title: Curriculum
curriculum_sections.body: Foundations: Cell Biology, Anatomy & Physiology • Students are introduced to the fundamentals of medicine and healthcare practice, learning the theoretical foundations of key medical specialties. • Clinical Skills & Simulation Labs • Hands-on simulations in the simulator lab: digital anatomy, suturing, blood draws and BLS, plus the fundamentals of doctor-patient interaction. • Imaging, Research & Clinical Case • AI in medical imaging, reading X-ray, CT, MRI and ultrasound, alongside medical research and a deep dive into the admission process for Italian medical universities. • Special Excursions • Milan sightseeing and a Lake Como excursion, plus a pizza night beyond the classroom. • Final Project • The program culminates in a capstone: students solve and present their own clinical case.

curriculum_sections.title: Program highlights
curriculum_sections.body: Explore anatomy, physiology, radiology, surgery and lab medicine • Hands-on simulation labs: digital anatomy, suturing, blood draws and BLS • Capstone: solve and present your own clinical case

learning_outcomes: Explore anatomy, physiology, radiology, surgery and lab medicine
Hands-on simulation labs: digital anatomy, suturing, blood draws and BLS
Capstone: solve and present your own clinical case

title: Pet Design
subject: Design
description_short: Design for animals with The HAD: from ethology and sketching to a finished product you build yourself.
description_full: This pet design summer program in Milan runs for two weeks and is designed for students aged 15 to 18. Designed for creative students curious about design, animals, veterinary and the fast-growing pet industry. Hosted in Milan in partnership with The HAD - Human Animal Design®, Italy’s leading studio in Pet Design, this two-week program introduces an entirely new discipline: designing products, spaces and services for the well-being of pets. Combining design, ethology and zoo-anthropology, students learn to design not for humans alone, but for the animals who share our world, culminating in their own multiexperiential concept for the pet industry. The program takes place in Milan, the global capital of design and home to The HAD - Human Animal Design®, the studio that pioneered Pet Design as a discipline. Here students work at the meeting point of two of Italy’s great strengths, world-class design culture and a deep respect for animal welfare, in a city that hosts Salone del Mobile, Milan Design Week and the ADI Design Museum.

curriculum_sections.title: Curriculum
curriculum_sections.body: Design, Ethology & Zoo-Anthropology • Move beyond an anthropocentric approach and study the foundations of relational ethology and zoo-anthropology, learning how to design ethically for pets. • Animal Perception, Physiology & Needs • Explore the perception, physiology and behavioural needs of dogs and cats, and apply design thinking to real case studies. • Human-Animal Design Studio & Project • Work at the meeting point of design culture and animal welfare with The HAD - Human Animal Design®, turning research into a designed solution. • Special Excursions • Company visit at Arcaplanet and MyPet Clinic, the ADI Design Museum and a Lake Como excursion (residential only), plus Milan sightseeing, visits to Italian design brands and a gelato afternoon. • Final Project • The program culminates in a capstone: students design their own multiexperiential solution, a product, space or service for the pet industry.

curriculum_sections.title: Program highlights
curriculum_sections.body: Learn the foundations of pet design, relational ethology and zoo-anthropology • Explore the perception, physiology and behavioural needs of dogs and cats • Design a multiexperiential product, space or service for the pet industry

learning_outcomes: Learn the foundations of pet design, relational ethology and zoo-anthropology
Explore the perception, physiology and behavioural needs of dogs and cats
Design a multiexperiential product, space or service for the pet industry

title: Sports Management
subject: Business
description_short: How Italian sport is run: club management, fan growth and team strategy, pitched to a panel of mentors.
description_full: This sports management summer program in Milan runs for two weeks and is designed for students aged 15 to 18. Discover how the business of sport really works, inside two of the industries Italy leads the world in: football and motorsport. Over two weeks, students go behind the commercial engine of professional sport: how a top football club and a professional racing team are financed, how players and drivers are contracted, sponsored and turned into global brands, and how championships and events are built and sold. Taught by faculty who work inside leading sports organizations, with an HQ visit to a top Serie A club and behind-the-scenes access at a live GT race weekend. The program is based in Milan, home turf of both industries: Serie A football and the €12.4bn Motor Valley, home to 188 racing teams.

curriculum_sections.title: Curriculum
curriculum_sections.body: The Business of Football: Clubs, Players and Revenue • Week 1 covers club economics, player contracts and the transfer system, the academy model and commercial operations. • The Business of Motorsport: Teams, Drivers & Sponsorship • Week 2 covers team economics and the sponsorship model, the anatomy of a team, driver management and how championships are commercialized. • Team Project: Grow a Club, Launch a Team • Two team projects bring it to life: grow a top club’s fanbase and launch a new racing team, each pitched to a mentor panel. • Special Excursions • HQ visit of a leading Serie A team, GT race weekend, visit to a leading sports apparel brand and Lake Como. • Final Project • The program culminates in two team projects: growing a top club’s fanbase and launching a new racing team, each pitched to a mentor panel.

curriculum_sections.title: Program highlights
curriculum_sections.body: Football club economics, player contracts and the transfer system • Motorsport team economics, driver management and the sponsorship model • Two team projects: grow a club’s fanbase and launch a new racing team

learning_outcomes: Football club economics, player contracts and the transfer system
Motorsport team economics, driver management and the sponsorship model
Two team projects: grow a club’s fanbase and launch a new racing team

title: Motorsport Management
subject: Business
description_short: How a racing series is run, with SRO Motorsports Group and a day inside the paddock.
description_full: This motorsport management summer term in Milan and the Motor Valley runs for two weeks and is designed for undergraduate and master students. Motorsport Management & Leadership is a two-week summer experience for university students who want a career in the business and leadership of motor racing. Not a degree or a multi-year commitment, it is the most immersive way into the industry while you are still studying, open to far more people than a postgraduate program. You learn the sport where it lives: Italy’s Motor Valley and Lombardy, where the cars are built, the teams are based and the championships are run. Across two weeks you go inside how a motorsport business runs: financing, sponsorship, media rights, talent management, and how winning teams are led under pressure, taught on the ground by the people who run the sport, led by SRO Motorsports Group, creator of modern GT racing. It blends seminars with factory visits, a live race weekend, a leadership module and The Brief: a real commercial challenge pitched to industry decision-makers. Ideal for Business, Management, Sports Management, Marketing, Economics and Automotive Engineering students. The program is taught inside motorsport’s heartland, Italy’s Motor Valley and Lombardy, where the cars are built, the teams are based and the championships are run. The Motor Valley generates around €12bn and is home to 188 racing teams and constructors, including Ferrari, Lamborghini, Pagani, Dallara, Maserati and Ducati. And the timing matters: motorsport is in its strongest decade, with Formula 1 posting record revenue of $3.87bn in 2025 and sponsorship passing 20% of core revenue for the first time, making commercial and leadership roles some of the most in-demand in the sport.

curriculum_sections.title: Curriculum
curriculum_sections.body: The Economics & Commerce of Motorsport • How teams are financed (budgets, cost caps, prize money, the sponsorship model), how sponsorship and media rights are sold and activated, how championships are commercialised and how drivers are managed as brands. • Leadership, Performance & The Team • How a race team is structured and led under pressure, the engineer-to-leader path, and Pit Wall, a live strategy simulation. • Race Weekend & Commercial Challenge Pitch • Behind-the-scenes access at a live race weekend and a Motor Valley visit, closing with The Brief, a real commercial challenge pitched to industry decision-makers. • Special Excursions • Dallara HQ visit, race weekend paddock access and a Ferrari factory visit including Corse Clienti and Scuderia Ferrari. • The Brief • A real commercial challenge, pitched to industry decision-makers at the end of the two weeks.

curriculum_sections.title: Program highlights
curriculum_sections.body: Team economics, finance, sponsorship, commercial and media rights • Leadership, high performance teams and Pit Wall, a live strategy simulation • A live race weekend and The Brief, a real commercial challenge pitch

learning_outcomes: Team economics, finance, sponsorship, commercial and media rights
Leadership, high performance teams and Pit Wall, a live strategy simulation
A live race weekend and The Brief, a real commercial challenge pitch

title: AgriFoodTech
subject: Health & Life Sciences
description_short: The future of food and farming, from vertical farms and labs to the companies bringing it to market.
description_full: This agrifood and agritech summer program in Milan, Piacenza and Turin runs for two weeks and is designed for students aged 15 to 18. A two-week program for students aged 15 to 18, exploring how food is produced, kept safe and reinvented, from laboratory science to the technologies transforming farming and the supply chain. The program runs between Milan, Piacenza and Turin, combining lessons and laboratory work with visits to leading Italian food innovation companies. It builds toward a Food Innovation Project developed and presented by the students.

curriculum_sections.body: Food Science & Safety • Study the science behind food production, quality and safety, with laboratory work on ingredients and the standards that protect the supply chain. • AgriTech: Farming, Traceability & Blockchain • Explore the technologies transforming agriculture, from precision and vertical farming to traceability systems and blockchain applied to the food supply chain. • Food Innovation Project • Work in teams on a food innovation project, developing an idea from concept to a final presentation. • Special Excursions • Visits to leading Italian food innovation companies, a Lake Como excursion, Milan sightseeing and a pizza night. • Final Project • The program culminates in the Food Innovation Project: students develop and present their own concept, applying what they have learned across food science and AgriTech.

curriculum_sections.title: Program highlights
curriculum_sections.body: Study food science, safety and quality across the supply chain • Explore AgriTech: precision farming, traceability and blockchain • Build a food innovation project from concept to final pitch

Explore AgriTech: precision farming, traceability and blockchain

title: Motorsport Engineering
subject: Engineering
description_short: A university-level term inside Dallara’s engineering facility, with an optional curricular internship.
description_full: This motorsport engineering summer term in the Motor Valley runs for two weeks and is designed for undergraduate and master students. A two-week summer term that fills the motorsport gap most engineering degrees leave open. In the heart of Italy’s Motor Valley, university engineering students go deep into both sides of the sport: Race Car Design & Manufacturing, designing, building and validating a real aerodynamic component and Race Strategy & Performance, learning the race engineer’s craft from active Formula 1 race engineers and running a full race weekend. Deliberately advanced, hands-on, and taught entirely in English. Ideal for Mechanical, Automotive, Aerospace and Motorsport Engineering students. The program is based in the Motor Valley (Emilia-Romagna), at a leading engineering and innovation campus near Parma. description_full: Children are already experts at asking why. Big Questions Club gives that curiosity a place to grow through stories, puzzles, mystery objects, movement, drawing, and role-play. As students explore questions about fairness, friendship, rules, and how we know what is true, they learn to explain what they think, listen to ideas, and discover how a thoughtful question can lead somewhere unexpected. Each day turns one big idea into something students can see and do. They might act out ways to share materials, follow instructions like a paper robot, sort clues to decide what can be known, or build a gallery around what makes something beautiful. Students can participate through speaking, drawing, acting, or building, making the course welcoming to different ways of participating. In the final week, each student chooses a favorite question and creates a Big Questions Gallery project. A poster, comic, model, or interactive display presents two possible answers, the student’s current view, and the reasons behind it. Students also complete an illustrated Big Questions journal and share their finished work in a supportive setting. description_full: A secret message is a mathematical puzzle with a purpose. Students trace cryptography from Caesar shifts and substitution systems to the Enigma machine and the public-key ideas that protect modern communication. Each new cipher reveals both an encoding strategy and a weakness a codebreaker can exploit. Hands-on challenges include building cipher wheels, encrypting and decrypting partner messages, using frequency analysis, and testing Vigenère and Polybius-based systems. Students connect those activities to modular arithmetic, matrices, prime factorization, number theory, and the way computers represent information. Historical cases show how cryptanalysis influenced events and how security standards change when technology advances. For the capstone, students design and analyze an original cryptographic system or complete an in-depth cryptanalysis project. They document the key, method, mathematical reasoning, strengths, limitations, and evidence from testing, then present their findings to the class. description_full: Why does a plant have tall stems, purple flowers or jagged leaves? Students begin with real plants and seeds, then investigate the tiny instructions behind those visible traits. They plant fast-growing seeds, track changes in a journal and watch colored water travel through celery stems. The class moves from plant parts into genetics. Students extract DNA from strawberries, build a double-helix model with paired bases and compare inherited traits with learned traits. They open soaked beans to find the embryo, seed coat and cotyledon, explore pollination and group plants into families by shared features. Each student invents a plant with its own DNA pattern, traits, habitat and helpful mutation. They develop the idea through capstone checkpoints, rehearse their explanation and present the finished model during a Plant Genetics Showcase. description_full: Which paper airplane flies farthest? Is there really more of one candy color in the bag? Students become data detectives, using numbers as clues to answer questions through games and hands-on experiments. They sort candies, measure rolling balls, compare basketball scores, and test their predictions with classmates. The discoveries take shape in colorful graphs and simple tables. Students explore averages, middle values, and numbers that appear most often, then notice how much results change from one try to the next. Dice and spinner games introduce chance. Class surveys show how asking a question differently can change someone’s answer, while weather observations reveal patterns over time. For their final detective project, students choose something they want to find out. They make a prediction, gather information, create graphs, and share what they discovered. The fun is in following the clues, finding surprises, and explaining the answer in their own words. description_full: A courtroom argument must connect a claim to evidence and explain why that evidence matters. Students practice that structure through the claim, warrant, data and impact model, then learn how voice, pacing, questioning and listening affect whether an argument is understood. A scripted Goldilocks trial introduces courtroom roles and procedure. Students write openings, develop a case theory, prepare direct and cross-examinations, practice objections and compare open-ended questions with leading questions. SPAR debates require teams to argue assigned positions and respond to critique, helping students test ideas before the final trial. The capstone turns the events of the book Holes into a child-labor case involving Camp Green Lake. Prosecution and defense teams research the text, organize admissible evidence, assign attorneys and witnesses, prepare questions and anticipate opposing claims. During the final mock trial, students deliver openings and closings, question witnesses, raise objections and perform their assigned courtroom roles. This three-week course is part of Summer Discovery’s Institute for the Gifted program on Bryn Mawr College’s campus in Bryn Mawr, Pennsylvania. The program is available to commuter students. Beyond class, students take part in campus activities, make new friends, and build confidence and independence in a college setting.

description_full: Microorganisms are everywhere, but their effects range from helpful to harmful. Students begin with the history of medical microbiology and the scientists whose discoveries changed how people understand infection. A Glo Germ investigation makes transmission visible and gives students evidence for testing a handwashing protocol. The course compares bacteria, viruses, fungi, and other microbes, then connects them to immune-system responses, infectious disease, microbiomes, and biotechnology. Students sort microbes by function, map immune cells involved in different disorders, research how a treatment affects a disease process, and communicate findings through diagrams and short presentations. For the capstone, students identify a challenge or opportunity where microorganisms play an important role. They investigate the underlying biology, current approaches, and emerging trends, then propose a scientifically grounded response. Checkpoints guide research, evidence, and presentation so the final project explains both the problem and the microbiological reasoning behind the solution. This three-week course is part of Summer Discovery’s Institute for the Gifted program on Bryn Mawr College’s campus in Bryn Mawr, Pennsylvania. The program is available to commuter students. Beyond class, students take part in campus activities, make new friends, and build confidence and independence in a college setting.

description_full: Choosing a stock is only the beginning. Students ask what makes a company worth investigating, how an investor’s goals shape strategy, and why return cannot be considered without risk, fees, and time. The course makes financial ideas visible through articles, videos, group analysis, and portfolio work. Students compare stock-picking criteria, use free screeners, examine company profiles and financial ratios, and build a hypothetical portfolio. As prices change, they calculate return on investment, review allocation choices, and consider how taxes, commissions, interest rates, and different risk profiles affect an outcome. The capstone brings those decisions into one investment presentation. Students document the companies and industries selected, explain their allocation, create a portfolio graphic, track performance, and defend the reasoning behind changes. Students compare results with classmates and revise their reasoning. The goal is not to predict the market. It is to practice making informed choices and explaining the evidence behind them. This three-week course is part of Summer Discovery’s Institute for the Gifted program on Bryn Mawr College’s campus in Bryn Mawr, Pennsylvania. The program is available to commuter students. description_full: The ocean connects tiny plankton, enormous marine mammals, coastal communities, and the global climate. Students investigate life from coral reefs to the ocean floor while asking how organisms are adapted to water, food webs, temperature, depth, and one another. Experiments and research make ocean systems tangible. Students test density, model the water cycle, examine ocean chemistry, and compare evolutionary and ecological relationships among marine plants and animals. They research a chosen organism, communicate its adaptations, and consider how temperature change, pollution, fishing, habitat loss, or other human activity may affect it. For the capstone, students investigate a marine issue and its effects on local animals, plants, and people. They propose a solution designed to benefit both communities and the environment, then plan how it could gain funding, supplies, or public support. A mock-election presentation asks them to defend the evidence and practicality behind the proposal. Using Microsoft MakeCode and Finch robots, students create sequences, control motion, test lights and sound, and adjust programs after observing what the robot actually does. Creative engineering adds a second challenge: a model must stand, move, or communicate an idea. Students sketch, build, test, and improve three-dimensional characters and story elements. Mind maps, sequencing activities, and oral storytelling help them connect physical design to a clear beginning, middle, and end. For the capstone, students develop an original superhero story and create a visual or 3D model that brings the character and imaginary world to life. Checkpoints guide character development, plot structure, construction, revision, and rehearsal. Students present the finished story, share their visual, and explain how their creative choices support the narrative. This three-week course is part of Summer Discovery’s Institute for the Gifted program on Bryn Mawr College’s campus in Bryn Mawr, Pennsylvania. The program is available to commuter students. Beyond class, students take part in campus activities, make new friends, and build confidence trying something new.

description_full: A toothpick tower must stand tall without toppling. A pizza-box oven must capture enough heat to work. Students tackle playful challenges like these by taking objects apart, putting them together, and thinking with their hands. Along the way, they use ideas from science, engineering, math, and art to plan and create original designs. Students investigate ancient and modern engineering wonders and explore how chemical, civil, electrical, and mechanical engineers solve different problems. Geometry helps them plan structures, while experiments with heat, materials, and physical forces show how a design behaves. Each challenge gives students a chance to build, test, notice what happened, and try again. For the capstone, students choose a real-world concern connected to one of the engineering branches they explored. They design a solution as a model, prototype, detailed blueprint, or original product, then explain their engineering choices to classmates. This three-week course is part of Summer Discovery’s Institute for the Gifted program on Bryn Mawr College’s campus in Bryn Mawr, Pennsylvania. The program is available to commuter students. Beyond class, students take part in campus activities, make new friends, and build confidence trying something new.

description_full: How do the brain, body, and environment work together to shape attention, stress, perception, and behavior? Students build a foundation in neuroanatomy and neural function while exploring the emerging field of environmental neuroscience. Hands-on activities make the science tangible. Students use an interactive brain atlas, build and label a neuron, test perception and attention, practice breathing techniques, and examine how habits and circadian rhythms affect well-being. A guided walk in Pine Park turns attention restoration into a field observation, while a sheep brain lab connects models and anatomy. A visit to Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center introduces clinical and research settings connected with neurology, neuroimaging, psychiatry, or rehabilitation. In small groups, students then develop a research question and present a capstone project that connects neuroscience evidence with a topic they want to explore in greater depth. This two-week full-day academy is part of Dartmouth Precollege Summer Scholars. Students spend the full program focused on one intensive academy. The academy is available to residential students and will take place both on Dartmouth's main campus as well as the legendary mountain retreat, Moosilauke Ravine Lodge, where outdoor experiences become part of the learning and development. Beyond class, students connect focused academic work with campus life, growing independence, and clearer direction about what students may want to study or pursue next. The program is developed and academically led by Dartmouth.

description_full: Students study how finance, accounting, economics, marketing, strategy, and communication work together inside a modern business. Instead of treating each subject as a separate unit, the course uses one collaborative public-company valuation project to connect the ideas. Case studies, spreadsheets, financial analysis, and group discussions help students examine how companies identify customers, generate revenue, finance growth, compete, manage risk, and evaluate new opportunities. Teams interpret business information and apply it to both organizational choices and familiar personal-finance questions. The project culminates in a presentation of findings and analysis supported by data and financial reasoning. Students explain their assumptions and show how market forces, innovation, strategy, and risk can affect a company’s value. The valuation gives the academy a common thread. New ideas in accounting, markets, customers, and strategy are tested against the same company, helping students see how one change in an assumption can alter both the analysis and the conclusion. This two-week full-day academy is part of Dartmouth Precollege Summer Scholars. Students spend the full program focused on one intensive academy. The academy is available to residential and commuter students. Beyond class, students connect focused academic work with campus life, growing independence, and clearer direction about what students may want to study or pursue next. The program is developed and academically led by Dartmouth.

curriculum_sections.body: • Study foundations in accounting, finance, economics, marketing, and strategy • Analyze how a public company serves customers and generates revenue • Build and interpret a spreadsheet-based valuation model • Evaluate investment opportunities, risk, competition, and growth • Apply financial reasoning to business and personal-finance decisions • Collaborate on a public-company analysis • Present professional findings supported by data

curriculum_sections.title: Learning outcomes
curriculum_sections.body: By the end of the course, students will be able to: • Explain how core business functions contribute to company decisions and value • Use financial analysis and market evidence to evaluate a public company • Present collaborative findings with clear quantitative reasoning Students leave with a completed company valuation and presentation, stronger business judgment, and clearer direction about finance, economics, marketing, management, or entrepreneurship.

Participants should be ready to work with spreadsheets and quantitative information, discuss case studies, collaborate on a company analysis, and present their findings. Careful reasoning, comfort asking questions, and a willingness to explain assumptions will be more important than arriving with specialized knowledge.

description_full: Students examine the technologies, policies, and ethical choices shaping the transition to a lower-carbon future. The course brings together climate science, engineering, economics, philosophy, medicine, and public policy so that energy decisions are considered from several angles. Students calculate personal carbon footprints, interpret emissions data, compare energy technologies, and debate climate policy. Case studies and collaborative projects ask them to connect individual choices with infrastructure, economics, air quality, environmental justice, and public action. A carbon-tax versus cap-and-trade simulation asks students to negotiate from the perspectives of governments, businesses, citizens, and nongovernmental organizations. Guest speakers and a visit to Dartmouth’s Bone Lab add perspectives from climate science, environmental anthropology, medicine, ecology, agriculture, and sustainability. Students are asked to distinguish a promising technology from a complete climate strategy. Their final project must address emissions, cost, feasibility, equity, policy, infrastructure, and human behavior in a realistic decarbonization plan for a community or system they know. This two-week full-day academy is part of Dartmouth Precollege Summer Scholars. Students spend the full program focused on one intensive academy. The academy is available to residential and commuter students. Beyond class, students connect focused academic work with campus life, growing independence, and clearer direction about what students may want to study or pursue next. The program is developed and academically led by Dartmouth.

curriculum_sections.body: • Calculate and interpret personal and community carbon footprints • Compare energy mixes, costs, storage options, and emissions • Analyze climate-health and environmental-justice case studies • Debate ethical, economic, and policy questions • Take part in a carbon-tax versus cap-and-trade simulation • Learn from visiting scientists and sustainability professionals • Design and present an evidence-based decarbonization strategy

curriculum_sections.body: By the end of the course, students will be able to: • Analyze sources of carbon emissions and interpret relevant environmental evidence • Evaluate energy technologies and policy choices across scientific, economic, and ethical dimensions • Design and communicate an evidence-based decarbonization strategy Students leave with a completed sustainability proposal, stronger interdisciplinary reasoning, and clearer direction about environmental science, engineering, policy, economics, or climate research.

Participants should be ready to work with data, make calculations, discuss contested policy questions respectfully, take part in simulations and case studies, and collaborate on a decarbonization strategy. Curiosity about how science and public decisions interact will help students engage deeply.

description_full: Students study why international conflicts begin, how they end, and what diplomats and institutions can do when interests collide. Case studies and current events introduce civil war, peacekeeping, negotiation, and the role of the United Nations in international security. Research and simulation place students inside the problem. They evaluate sources, compare stakeholder positions, identify trade-offs, build coalitions, and draft resolutions. Library research and guest speakers from Dartmouth’s Dickey Center for International Understanding connect the work to international-affairs practice. The academy culminates in a United Nations Security Council simulation focused on conflicts in Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Somalia. Representing member states, students prepare briefings, draft resolutions, negotiate agreements, and respond to questions while balancing their assigned country’s priorities. Preparation for the simulation is cumulative. Research defines each state's interests, drafted language makes proposals precise, and live negotiation reveals which goals are essential and where compromise is possible. The final crisis response tests all three at once. This two-week full-day academy is part of Dartmouth Precollege Summer Scholars. Students spend the full program focused on one intensive academy. The academy is available to residential and commuter students. Beyond class, students connect focused academic work with campus life, growing independence, and clearer direction about what students may want to study or pursue next. curriculum_sections.title: Learning outcomes
curriculum_sections.body: By the end of the course, students will be able to: • Explain how negotiation and conflict-resolution strategies apply to international crises • Find and evaluate sources for research in international affairs • Draft, present, and negotiate resolutions in a UN Security Council simulation Students leave with researched resolutions and simulation experience, stronger negotiation and communication skills, and clearer direction about international relations, policy, law, or diplomacy.

Respectful disagreement, careful preparation, and comfort discussing serious real-world conflicts are essential.

description_full: Dartmouth’s outdoor spaces become both subject and classroom as students explore how place can shape voice, imagination, and memory. Guided walks, meditation, close observation, and daily writing exercises turn encounters with the natural world into material for original work. Students experiment with poetry, short fiction, and creative nonfiction. Readings and lessons in imagery, metaphor, voice, sensory detail, point of view, and narrative structure give them tools for developing drafts. Writing sessions in places such as Pine Park, Occum Pond, BEMA, and the Robert Frost site provide changing settings and perspectives. Collaborative workshops add the discipline of revision. Students share work, give constructive feedback, decide what to change, and assemble a small portfolio of revised pieces. A closing reading gives them the chance to present selected work to the class. The outdoor setting is used as a source of specific observation, not simply a backdrop. Students return to their notes and drafts throughout the academy, noticing how a change in form, detail, or point of view can reshape the same experience. This two-week full-day academy is part of Dartmouth Precollege Summer Scholars. Students spend the full program focused on one intensive academy. description_full: Students experience engineering as a cycle of defining a problem, building a possible solution, testing it, and using evidence to improve the design. Challenges require attention to user needs, feasibility, durability, efficiency, sustainability, safety, and cost rather than a single ideal answer. Teams spend at least 40% of the academy building and testing. They compare materials through stiffness, impact, friction, and wear tests; create two prototype versions; collect measurements; identify failure modes; and use the evidence to decide what to change. Entrepreneurship is integrated throughout the process. Students define a value proposition, estimate cost of goods sold, compare alternatives, consider manufacturing and lifecycle impacts, and explain why a design is worth pursuing. A technical dossier, poster, slide deck, live demonstration, and founder-style pitch document the finished work. Each testing cycle creates a record of engineering judgment. Students compare what they expected with what happened, identify the most important failure or constraint, and use that evidence to decide which change is most likely to improve the next version. This two-week full-day academy is part of Dartmouth Precollege Summer Scholars. Students spend the full program focused on one intensive academy. The academy is available to residential and commuter students. Beyond class, students connect focused academic work with campus life, growing independence, and clearer direction about what students may want to study or pursue next. curriculum_sections.title: Learning outcomes
curriculum_sections.body: By the end of the course, students will be able to: • Create and refine a functional prototype through evidence-based build-test-learn cycles • Use material tests, performance data, and failure analysis to justify design decisions • Communicate a solution through a technical dossier, poster, live demonstration, and founder-style pitch Students leave with two prototype versions and several portfolio-ready artifacts, stronger technical problem-solving skills, and clearer direction about engineering, product design, materials, manufacturing, or entrepreneurship.

Students must bring a personal laptop, and closed-toe shoes are required in shop spaces.

description_full: Students begin as problem finders. Innovation sprints move teams through design thinking, customer discovery, rapid prototyping, testing, and venture modeling. Each venture decision must connect back to evidence from people affected by the problem. Teams use that evidence to narrow the opportunity, strengthen the prototype, and explain how their model could create value while remaining responsible, realistic, and open to future iteration. description_full: Students explore how hedge funds, private-equity firms, venture-capital investors, and institutional portfolios operate in global financial markets. The course begins with risk, return, diversification, compounding, and portfolio construction before comparing alternative assets with traditional investments. Case studies, simulations, market data, and discussion ask students to evaluate strategies, opportunities, and risk. They also examine how economics, politics, history, and behavioral factors can influence investor decisions and market outcomes. Guest perspectives from Dartmouth alumni, Tuck School of Business faculty, and finance professionals connect concepts with careers and current industry questions. Students finish by analyzing and presenting an investment case with a clear explanation of the evidence and trade-offs. Students compare strategies from the perspective of an investor responsible for an entire portfolio, not a single winning idea. That frame makes liquidity, diversification, time horizon, and risk central to the analysis and keeps market excitement in context. This two-week full-day academy is part of Dartmouth Precollege Summer Scholars. Students spend the full program focused on one intensive academy. The academy is available to residential and commuter students. Beyond class, students connect focused academic work with campus life, growing independence, and clearer direction about what students may want to study or pursue next. The program is developed and academically led by Dartmouth.

curriculum_sections.body: • Study risk, return, diversification, compounding, and portfolio construction • Compare hedge funds, private equity, venture capital, and traditional investments • Analyze simplified investment cases and market data • Participate in market or portfolio simulations • Evaluate economic, political, and behavioral influences • Learn from alumni, faculty, and finance professionals • Present an investment analysis with risks and trade-offs

curriculum_sections.title: Learning outcomes
curriculum_sections.body: By the end of the course, students will be able to: • Explain how major alternative investment strategies differ in purpose and risk • Analyze an investment case using financial reasoning and market evidence • Evaluate portfolio decisions in light of economic, political, and behavioral factors Students leave with a completed investment analysis, stronger financial literacy, and clearer direction about finance, economics, consulting, business, or investment management.

description_full: Students explore the continuum of healthcare, beginning with prevention and wellness and extending through emergency response and acute care. Case studies, clinical demonstrations, simulations, and conversations with healthcare professionals show how modern systems respond to different patient needs. Topics include preventative medicine, nutrition, epidemiology, public health, diagnostic reasoning, emergency medicine, trauma care, and patient communication. Simulated scenarios ask students to interpret evidence, prioritize next steps, and explain decisions under pressure. The course also examines teamwork across medicine. Students compare the roles of physicians, nurses, emergency responders, therapists, researchers, and public-health professionals, then reflect on how scientific skill, communication, and compassion contribute to patient outcomes. Students move between the perspective of an individual patient and that of a community. This helps them see where prevention, public health, emergency response, and clinical care overlap, and why effective healthcare depends on both specialized knowledge and coordinated action. This two-week, full-day intensive academy is part of Dartmouth Precollege Summer Scholars in Hanover, New Hampshire. The academy is fully developed and run by Dartmouth and taught by Dartmouth faculty and expert instructors. Residential and commuter students participate throughout the day, pairing focused academic work with campus life and growing independence.

curriculum_sections.title: Learning outcomes
curriculum_sections.body: By the end of the course, students will be able to: • Explain how prevention, public health, and emergency medicine connect across the care continuum • Apply evidence and clinical reasoning to simulated patient scenarios • Communicate and collaborate while recognizing the roles of different healthcare professionals Students leave with patient-case and simulation experience, stronger clinical reasoning and teamwork skills, and clearer direction about medicine, nursing, public health, emergency care, or biomedical science.

Participants should be ready to work through patient scenarios, make decisions with a team, communicate clearly, and discuss the responsibilities of different healthcare roles. description_full: Students explore how the brain shapes memory, attention, perception, learning, emotion, decision-making, habits, and mental health. Interactive lectures, case studies, demonstrations, and guest speakers introduce major questions in psychology and cognitive neuroscience. Hands-on activities make abstract concepts easier to see. Students observe an EEG demonstration, build a neuron, use prism goggles to investigate perception, examine a brain-computer interface, and take part in a sheep brain dissection. Tours of Dartmouth’s greenhouse and sports complex add settings for discussing the connections among environment, performance, and well-being. The course also examines research ethics and the methods scientists use to study the brain and behavior. Visits, guest lectures, and conversations about careers show how psychology and neuroscience connect with medicine, education, law, child development, and neural disorders. In small groups, students choose a psychology or cognitive neuroscience topic, research it in greater depth, and create a 12-minute capstone presentation. Peer feedback helps them strengthen both the substance and delivery of their work. This two-week full-day academy is part of Dartmouth Precollege Summer Scholars. Students spend the full program focused on one intensive academy. The academy is available to residential and commuter students. Beyond class, students connect focused academic work with campus life, growing independence, and clearer direction about what students may want to study or pursue next. The program is developed and academically led by Dartmouth.
